finding.problem: A selected mutable package artifact could change during the first successful drain or a fresh tool grant callback, then be recaptured as new package authority.
finding.observed_initial: Both mutation variants caused a second package evaluator call with changed private metadata and an actual child write; unchanged control forwarded.
finding.repair: Check the original selected package authority after successful drain and again after fresh tool preparation, before recapturing the package artifact.
finding.observed_fixed: Both mutation variants make exactly one original package evaluation, no child write, and fixed tool_call_authority_changed. Unchanged control forwards.
finding.status: fixed in the exact reviewed source

reviewed_boundaries: Complete plain JSON request ownership and immutable final frame remain selected by explicit tool intent and object identity.
Authority binds exact complete supported config/context/catalog and actual artifact data, including private metadata, before grant/browser/saved lookup and claim callbacks.
A private evaluator returned copy is validated against the source artifact and the object actually consumed receives its own binding.
Nested invocation scopes restore prior checks; final ordinary/package forwarding receives the selected check explicitly.
Unsupported authority inside a proxy invocation is terminal; legacy unsupported direct Python helper behavior cannot remove final proxy guarding.
Post-claim refresh explicitly selects fresh tool/package authority; the original 5 ms catalog fence remains before the final frame.
Verified package rewrites keep original request binding as parent and bind replacement bytes.
No new authority check occurs after a completed write; existing detached argument receipt projection remains before forwarding.
scope_limits: Finite local independent correctness evidence only; no universal security clearance.
The scanner callback is an explicit fixed evaluation fixture. The child records JSON and returns forwarded; it does not run npm.
No performance measurement, hosted cohort, campaign/profile entrypoint, E/F reactivation, threshold change, security alert disposition, or RSP-100 qualification.
Root and implementation owner retain responsibility for broader integration, Desktop generation, repository checks, and hosted validation.
